outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Challenge of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
outline.description: This chapter introduces the landscape of Large Language Models (LLMs) in mathematics, highlighting the gap between closed-source giants and open-source models. It defines the DeepSeekMath project's goals, key benchmarks (MATH, GSM8K), and the fundamental challenges of structured reasoning.
subtopics: The state of mathematical reasoning in AI: From GPT-4 to Open Source
Key Benchmarks: MATH, GSM8K, and their significance
The limitations of current open-source models
Overview of DeepSeekMath: Goals and contributions
Introduction to Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and Program-of-Thought (PoT)

outline.description: This chapter details the data engineering pipeline used to create a high-quality, large-scale mathematical dataset. It covers the iterative process of mining Common Crawl, training classifiers for data selection, decontamination strategies, and the validation of data quality against existing corpora.
subtopics: Data Sources: Leveraging Common Crawl for math content
Iterative Data Selection Pipeline using fastText classifiers
Seed corpus construction and domain identification
Decontamination techniques to prevent benchmark leakage
Comparative analysis: DeepSeekMath vs. MathPile, OpenWebMath, and Proof-Pile-2
The impact of multilingual data (English and Chinese) on reasoning

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Pre-Training Strategies and Base Model Development
outline.description: This chapter explains the training methodology for DeepSeekMath-Base. It explores the hypothesis that code training enhances mathematical reasoning, analyzes the surprising ineffectiveness of arXiv papers for general math benchmarks, and presents the evaluation results of the base model.
subtopics: Initialization from DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B
The role of code training in mathematical reasoning (Code vs. General tokens)
Training dynamics: Two-stage vs. One-stage training approaches
Why arXiv papers may not improve general mathematical reasoning benchmarks
Evaluation metrics: Self-contained solutions vs. Tool-augmented reasoning
Performance analysis on English and Chinese benchmarks

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Supervised Fine-Tuning for Instruction Alignment
outline.description: This chapter covers the transition from a base model to an instruction-tuned model. It details the curation of diverse instruction datasets (CoT, PoT, Tool-integrated), the fine-tuning process, and how this stage prepares the model for reinforcement learning.
subtopics: Curating instruction tuning datasets: English and Chinese problems
Data formats: Chain-of-Thought, Program-of-Thought, and Tool-Integrated Reasoning (ToRA)
Training configuration for DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B
Benchmarking against proprietary models (GPT-4, Gemini) and open-source peers
The impact of tool use on problem-solving accuracy

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 5: Reinforcement Learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
